question_text: Write a short note on the theory of mutations.

steps.label: What mutations are
steps.why: A mutation is inheritable, which is what separates it from an ordinary change an organism acquires in its lifetime.
common_mistakes: Calling mutations gradual. They are sudden.
Leaving out that they are inheritable.
steps.memory_tip: Sudden, random and inherited — all three words matter.

steps.label: De Vries and his plant
steps.why: De Vries saw new forms appear in one generation, which is why he argued that evolution moves in jumps rather than by slow steps.
common_mistakes: Crediting Darwin with the mutation theory. Hugo de Vries proposed it.
Getting the plant wrong. It is the evening primrose.
steps.memory_tip: Hugo de Vries and the evening primrose, Oenothera lamarckiana.
steps.margin_note: Name the scientist and the plant together.
lines: The mutation theory was proposed by Hugo

steps.label: The four mutant forms
steps.why: Four clearly different plants appeared from one parent stock, and none of them was an intermediate.
common_mistakes: Giving the common names without the species names.
Naming only two of the four forms.
steps.memory_tip: Brevistylis, levifolia, gigas, nanella — short style, smooth leaf, giant, dwarf.
steps.margin_note: Write the four as a list with names beside them.
lines: He found four different forms of Oenothera
Darwin called mutations sports of nature.

steps.label: Salient features
steps.why: The theory says a new form arrives complete rather than being built up over generations, which is where it parts company with Darwin.
common_mistakes: Saying mutations accumulate over generations. The theory says they do not.
Leaving out that mutations still face natural selection.
steps.memory_tip: Discontinuous, not accumulated, full-fledged, still selected.
steps.margin_note: Four numbered features close the answer.
